title: Account-aware compliance triage for hosting-mode sensitive security asks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers frequently submit security & compliance asks that span different Redwood deployment surfaces (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private). Current routing is manual, slow, and often misses hosting-mode constraints (e.g., hosted API cannot satisfy certain DPA/KMS demands). This causes churn, long SLAs, and ineffective evidence bundles.

Goal: Build an account-aware, hosting-mode-sensitive triage playbook + lightweight scorer that routes incoming security requests into an operational lane and returns a recommended response SLA and evidence checklist. The scorer will combine account tier (trial/paid/enterprise), deployment mode(s) used by the customer, data residency constraints, contract phase, and questionnaire complexity to output: recommended lane, estimated time-to-resolution (days), required artifacts, and auto-draft reply for CS/AE.

Scope: PM-owned triage logic, UI in intake form for CS/AE to surface key variables, backend scorer prototype (serverless) that returns routing and evidence plan, and a short-runbook for triage owners. Integrations: Confluence evidence library, GitHub PR template for engineering tasks, and Console dashboard for monitoring triage times and fallthroughs.

Out of scope for this ticket: full LLM-assisted automated answers to questionnaires (future), end-to-end enforcement of contract clauses, and changes to contract/legal templates.
acceptance_criteria: Scorer prototype accepts account_id, hosting_mode_hint, contract_stage, questionnaire_size_estimate, and data_residency flags and returns a routing result and SLA estimate.
Routing result includes one of: 'auto-standard', 'concierge-evidence', 'legal-review', 'private-onboarding-only', or 'decline-hosted'.
CS/AE intake UI updated with hosting-mode and contract-stage fields; selection feeds scorer in demo environment.
Runbook (Confluence) published with sample responses and evidence checklist templates for each routing lane.
Dashboard panel (internal) added showing triage queue length, mean time-to-route, and percent fallthroughs to Legal/Eng.
Prototype validated with 5 recent customer requests and accuracy reviewed by Security and Legal (comments captured).
comments: 2026-02-12 - PM kickoff: Reviewed backlog and selected 12 representative past tickets for model input features (Aisha).
2026-02-18 - Security review: Suggested adding a 'model-sensitivity' hint to account for whether customers run PII-sensitive workloads (Zoe Chen - Security).
2026-02-22 - Eng sync: Prototype will be serverless function behind intake service; Eng requested concrete schema for fields (Marco).
2026-02-27 - Legal feedback: Contract_stage must include 'negotiation-with-exceptions' to flag custom DPAs; delayed acceptance criteria adjusted (Marta Gomez - Legal).
2026-03-01 - Demo with Solutions: Scorer routed 5 historical asks; three would have moved to 'concierge-evidence' instead of manual Slack escalation. Action: instrument triage logging (Marco).
decision: Adopt a deterministic weighted-scoring approach for MVP (no ML). Score weights: account_tier (x1.5), hosting_mode_constraint (x2), questionnaire_size (x1), contract_stage multiplier (x1.2), data_residency flag (x2). Rationale: predictable behavior for reviewers and simple explainability for Legal and CS.
tradeoffs: Deterministic rules are transparent but may require frequent tuning as product surfaces evolve.
Automating too aggressively risks misrouting high-risk asks to 'auto-standard' — mitigation: low threshold and manual override for Legal.
Adding more telemetry (model-sensitivity) requires engineering effort and potential privacy review before storage of signals.
